sources.entry: Watson - A CLI application for time tracking.

summary.one_liner: Watson is a command-line time tracker that records work sessions by project and tag and produces logs and reports.
summary.what_it_does: Watson lets you start and stop timed "frames" for a project, optionally with tags such as +cats, from the terminal. The stop command reports how long the session lasted, and the log command lists recent sessions grouped by day. Both log and the report command support filtering by project, tag, and date. The README says reports can be generated for clients. Installation is through Homebrew on OS X or pip (package td-watson) on other platforms. Running watson help lists the available commands.
use_cases: track time spent on projects from the command line
filter time entries by project, tag, or date
tag work sessions for later review
notable: Frames are started and stopped with simple commands such as watson start project +tag
log and report commands both support project, tag, and date filters
Installable with Homebrew on OS X or with pip as td-watson
Documentation is referenced for installation details and the full command list
caveats: README gives Homebrew install only for OS X; other platforms use pip
Full installation details and command reference are in external documentation, not the README
keywords: track how long i spend on projects
